subject: biology
title: Male and Female Organs
welcome_lead: Tour the reproductive organs that make sperm and eggs and prepare for new life.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on male and female reproductive organs.
final_note: You can now name the main reproductive organs and their jobs.

walkthroughs.body_html: The testes make sperm. Sperm ducts carry sperm to the penis. The penis delivers sperm into the female's body during reproduction.
The ovaries make eggs. Oviducts carry eggs to the uterus, where a baby can grow. The vagina leads from the uterus to outside the body.
Sperm swim through the vagina and uterus into the oviduct. There they may meet an egg. If one sperm fertilises the egg, a new life can begin.

options: Evaporation of sweat absorbs energy (latent heat) from the skin, lowering body temperature.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
Sweat is cold and directly cools the skin on contact.

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
